chapter_note: This chapter is essentially absent of cosmological substrate. The "three things" enumerated are sociological observations about Christian/religious practice in the editor's contemporary world — men called by Christ's name, sons named after him, oaths sworn by him and demons. This is editor-world mapping, not cosmos→cosmos correspondence. The remainder is Mani-as-Apostle discourse claiming apostolic succession and discussing his teaching mission ("apostles who came before me," "fellow-heir in the new aeon"). Heavy damage (75.9%) but the surviving content is uniformly editorial. The enumeration mimics substrate structure but applies to contemporary religious sociology — exactly the pattern-mimicry editorial seam pattern.
